title: Undefined Behavior in C – A Lost Cause?
summary:
C is a very stable programming language. This sometimes leads to the impression that nothing can be improved. This talk will try to correct this impression. I will give an overview about what is happening in the C world. In particular, I will cover the topic of undefined behavior in C and talk about existing and emerging compiler features related to undefined behavior and memory safety. With regard to the C standard, I will summarize the improvements made to ISO C 23 and give an outlook about what is currently planned for the next revision of the C standard. Finally, I will use the opportunity to explain how the standardization process works and how the kernel community could become more involved.

Martin Uecker
ja_summary:
・C言語における「未定義動作」への対策と、最新のコンパイラによるメモリ安全性向上について解説。
・ISO C23の改善点および次期規格に向けた展望を紹介。
・標準化プロセスを解説し、Linuxカーネルコミュニティの関与促進を提言。

その不合格率が、7月の51.1%から10月には13.4%まで下がっていた。ところがログを調べると、3モデルでレビューするはずが、10月は全209件で1モデルしか判定していなかった。
残りの2モデルは、すべて unknown（判定不能）。集計処理はそれを除外し、回答した1モデルだけで合否を決めていた。有効な判定が減っていることは、ゲートの異常として通知されていなかった。
指標としては良くなっていたので、私はそれを素...
ja_summary:
AIエージェントによるコードレビューの不合格率が大幅改善したと思いきや、実際は3つ中2つのモデルが機能せず、実質1つのモデルだけで判定していたことが判明した。
指標の改善を鵜呑みにしていたが、不具合を検知するアラートが機能しておらず、ゲートの異常を見逃す結果となった。
自動化ツールやAIの運用において、指標のみに頼らず、システム内部の稼働状況を継続的に監視する必要性が浮き彫りになった。

title: Anybody Can Generate Code. Can Your AI Ship It? - Devfest Hyderabad 2026
summary:
AI coding agents can generate entire features, refactor applications and write tests in minutes. But producing code is not the same as engineering software we can confidently ship.

What happens when we stop treating AI as a coding assistant and start treating it as an engineering team?

In this session, we'll build a custom AI engineering harness using Google's Gemini, Gemma and Antigravity ecosystem, combining local, open-source and cloud models based on task complexity, cost and privacy requirements.

We'll create specialized agents for architecture, implementation, testing, code review and performance engineering. Using repository-level rules, reusable agent skills, structured handoffs and model routing, we'll orchestrate these agents into a coordinated engineering swarm.

But the real challenge starts when the agents say they're done.

We'll build independent verification layers around AI-generated code: compilation, static analysis, automated tests, UI validation, performance benchmarks and runtime telemetry. Instead of trusting an agent's claim that a task is complete, our harness will collect real engineering evidence.

When an agent introduces a regression, the verification system will identify the failure, feed measurements back into the agent workflow and require another implementation-and-validation cycle before accepting the change.

We'll also explore how local Gemma models enable private and offline development workflows, when to escalate tasks to more capable cloud models, and how multilingual voice interfaces can make agent orchestration more accessible.

The result is more than an AI coding assistant. It's the foundation of a verifiable AI engineering system, with specialized agents, automated quality gates and measurable outcomes.

Anybody can generate code now. The harder question is: can your AI actually ship it?

title: Spec-Driven Development: Building AI Aligned Software Through Living Specifications
summary:
Artificial Intelligence is fundamentally transforming software development. As AI agents become increasingly capable of generating code, implementing features, and executing complex development tasks, the central challenge shifts from writing code to defining intent, controlling execution, verifying results, and preserving knowledge.

This presentation, delivered by Haim Michael at All Day AI 2026 on October 22, 2026, explores Spec-Driven Development (SDD) as an approach to building reliable, maintainable, and AI-aligned software systems.

The presentation begins by tracing the evolution beyond traditional code-first development and the limits of relying solely on vibe coding. Although vibe coding provides significant advantages for rapid experimentation and prototyping, professional software engineering requires reliability, traceability, and long-term maintainability.

A key limitation is the lack of durable institutional memory. When architectural decisions and requirements exist primarily within conversations with AI assistants, maintaining and evolving complex systems becomes increasingly challenging.

Spec-Driven Development addresses this challenge by introducing specifications as a shared foundation for humans and AI agents. Living specifications capture requirements, constraints, architectural decisions, and acceptance criteria, helping teams coordinate development while staying aligned with human intent.

The presentation explores how to implement this approach using Kiro IDE, an agentic development environment designed to support structured, specification-driven workflows.

Topics covered include:

Spec-Driven Development fundamentals: Understanding the role of living specifications in AI-assisted software engineering.

SDD versus vibe coding: Examining the differences between exploratory coding and structured professional development.

Kiro IDE: Exploring an agentic development environment and its specification-driven capabilities.

Steering documents: Providing AI agents with project context, architectural guidelines, and development standards.

Requirements, design, and tasks: Structuring the development process around explicit specifications, including EARS requirements and Mermaid diagrams.

Agent hooks: Automating recurring development activities, including security reviews, testing, code formatting, and documentation.

Subagents: Delegating specialized tasks to multiple AI agents.

Parallel task execution: Understanding task dependencies and coordinating concurrent execution.

Kiro Workflows: Orchestrating multiple AI agents using sequential steps, parallel execution, and iterative loops.

Cloud-based AI agents: Exploring continuously operating agents that support development, testing, monitoring, incident response, and other tasks.

Best practices: Keep specifications synchronized with implementation, maintain detailed steering documents, and choose appropriate orchestration strategies.

The presentation also discusses the importance of skills, powers, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers in extending the capabilities of AI-assisted development environments.

A central theme is the changing role of software developers. As code generation becomes increasingly inexpensive, developers move toward higher levels of abstraction, focusing on goals, architecture, requirements, constraints, and quality standards.

Rather than manually implementing every component, developers increasingly become orchestrators of AI agents, coordinating software creation through clear specifications and structured workflows.

The key message is that the future of professional software development is not simply about generating more code faster. It is about building the right software while maintaining control, traceability, reliability, and alignment with human intent.

These slides are intended for software developers, software architects, engineering managers, technical leaders, and anyone interested in understanding how AI agents and Spec-Driven Development are reshaping software engineering.

As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly capable of generating software, the traditional software development process is undergoing a fundamental transformation. The primary challenge is gradually shifting from writing code to clearly defining requirements, designing systems, maintaining control over AI-generated implementations, and orchestrating AI agents.

This seminar explores Spec-Driven Development (SDD) as an emerging approach to AI-assisted software engineering. Rather than relying on loosely structured prompts, as commonly happens with vibe coding, SDD places specifications at the center of the development process. These specifications capture human intent and guide implementation, testing, architectural decisions, and ongoing maintenance.

From Code-First to Spec-Driven Development: Understanding why AI-generated code changes the fundamental challenges of software engineering.

The Limitations of Vibe Coding: Exploring the challenges of traceability, reproducibility, maintainability, and preserving human intent.

Specifications as the Foundation: Using structured requirements, technical designs, and implementation tasks to guide AI-assisted development.

Kiro IDE and Its Ecosystem: Introducing Kiro IDE and its tools for agentic software development.

Steering Documents and Development Workflows: Providing AI agents with project context, development guidelines, and architectural constraints.

Best Practices: Maintaining specifications, steering documents, and development processes that support reliable AI-assisted software engineering.
